text:
KeyError raised when using df.loc with boolean mask on MultiIndex DataFrame

Using df.loc[mask] where mask is a boolean Series raises an unexpected KeyError instead of filtering rows correctly. This is a regression introduced in the latest commit.
label: bug

text:
Crash in pd.concat when DataFrames have incompatible ExtensionArray dtypes

pd.concat([df1, df2]) raises TypeError: cannot cast ExtensionArray to incompatible dtype. Both inputs have valid data but different nullable integer backing arrays. Expected: automatic upcasting or a clear error message.
label: bug

text:
IndexError when calling groupby().nth() on empty DataFrame

groupby().nth(0) raises IndexError: index 0 is out of bounds for axis 0 with size 0 when the DataFrame is empty. The method should return an empty DataFrame instead of crashing.
label: bug

text:
Wrong results from DataFrame.cov() when input contains NaN values

DataFrame.cov() returns incorrect covariance values when some columns contain NaN. The computation should drop NaN pairs but instead appears to include them, producing values that are inconsistent with numpy.cov() on the same data.
label: bug

text:
SettingWithCopyWarning triggered incorrectly on valid assignment after .loc selection

Assigning a value via df.loc[mask, 'col'] = value correctly modifies the original DataFrame, but pandas still raises SettingWithCopyWarning: A value is trying to be set on a copy. The warning is a false positive and should not be raised in this case.
label: bug

text:
read_parquet fails with ArrowInvalid error on files written by pyarrow 12+

After upgrading pyarrow to version 12, pd.read_parquet() raises ArrowInvalid: Parquet file is not valid. The same file reads correctly with pyarrow 11. This is a regression in the pyarrow compatibility layer.
label: bug

text:
DataFrame.rank() returns incorrect ranks when method='dense' and there are NaN values

When a column contains NaN values and rank(method='dense') is called, the ranks for non-NaN values are off by one compared to the expected output. The NaN handling logic appears to have a fencepost error.
label: bug

text:
to_csv() produces malformed output when DataFrame contains newline characters in string columns

Calling df.to_csv() when a string column contains embedded newline characters produces a CSV file that does not round-trip correctly through read_csv(). The newlines are not being properly quoted according to RFC 4180.
label: bug

text:
Unexpected OverflowError in pd.to_datetime when parsing timestamps near epoch boundaries

pd.to_datetime(ts_string) raises OverflowError: Python int too large to convert to C long for valid ISO 8601 timestamps that are within the representable nanosecond range. Expected: successful conversion without error.
label: bug

text:
Series.str.split(expand=True) raises ValueError on Series containing None values

Series.str.split(pat=',', expand=True) raises ValueError: Length mismatch when the Series contains None values mixed with strings that split into different numbers of parts. Splitting should produce NaN in the missing positions.
label: bug

text:
Add support for writing multiple sheets to an ExcelWriter in a single method call

Currently each sheet must be added with a separate to_excel() call inside a with ExcelWriter context. A new method ExcelWriter.write_sheets(dict_of_dataframes) would allow writing all sheets at once and simplify the common pattern of exporting a dict of DataFrames to an Excel workbook.
label: feature

text:
Request: add DataFrame.sample() support for stratified sampling by column

The current sample() method selects rows uniformly at random. Adding a stratify parameter similar to sklearn's train_test_split would allow users to draw samples that preserve the class distribution of a specified column without requiring manual groupby-then-sample logic.
label: feature

text:
Implement lazy evaluation mode for chained DataFrame operations

Adding a DataFrame.lazy() method that defers computation until an action (e.g., .collect()) is called — similar to polars' lazy API — would enable the optimizer to fuse and reorder operations, reducing intermediate allocations for long method chains.
label: feature

text:
Add inplace parameter to DataFrame.rename_axis()

DataFrame.rename_axis() currently returns a new DataFrame even when inplace=True is not supported. Adding inplace=True support would be consistent with other methods like rename() and sort_values() and reduce unnecessary copies in tight loops.
label: feature

text:
Enhancement: support reading from cloud storage paths in pd.read_csv() without fsspec

Requiring users to install fsspec and pass a storage_options dict to read from s3:// or gs:// paths adds friction. Adding lightweight built-in support for common cloud prefixes — similar to how pandas wraps pyarrow for Parquet — would improve the out-of-box cloud experience.
label: feature

text:
Request: add DataFrame.to_lance() for writing to Lance columnar format

Lance is increasingly adopted for ML dataset storage. A native pd.DataFrame.to_lance(path) and pd.read_lance(path) function pair would make pandas a first-class citizen in Lance-based pipelines, similar to to_parquet()/read_parquet().
label: feature

text:
Add vectorised string padding to Series.str with a pad_center() alias for str.center()

Series.str.center(width, fillchar) exists but is not well-known. Adding a str.pad_center() alias alongside clearer documentation would improve discoverability of string-padding operations in the str accessor namespace.
label: feature

text:
Add chunk_size parameter to DataFrame.to_sql() for batched inserts

Currently to_sql() inserts all rows in a single statement, which can timeout or exceed database limits for large DataFrames. Adding a chunk_size parameter to split inserts into batches would make large write operations reliable without requiring the user to loop manually.
label: feature

text:
Support DataFrame.query() with timezone-aware datetime comparisons via @local_var

Passing a timezone-aware datetime as a local variable in query() raises TypeError: Cannot compare tz-naive and tz-aware datetime-like objects. This comparison should work correctly when both sides are timezone-aware, allowing queries like df.query('ts > @cutoff') where cutoff is a tz-aware Timestamp.
label: feature

text:
Implement df.to_iceberg() for writing DataFrames to Apache Iceberg tables

Apache Iceberg is the dominant open table format for data lakes. A native to_iceberg() method — analogous to to_parquet() — would let pandas users write directly to Iceberg tables without bridging through pyiceberg manually.
label: feature

text:
Fix broken link to contributing guide in README — points to old GitHub issue templates

The CONTRIBUTING.md link on line 42 of README.md points to https://github.com/pandas-dev/pandas/blob/main/.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE which no longer exists. The correct URL is https://github.com/pandas-dev/pandas/blob/main/.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/bug_report.yml
label: docs

text:
Add worked example to DataFrame.melt() docstring for unpivoting multiple value columns

The melt() docstring shows only a trivial single-value-column example. A second example demonstrating value_vars with multiple columns and the resulting long-format DataFrame would answer the most common usage question without requiring a Stack Overflow lookup.
label: docs

text:
Docstring for pd.cut() incorrectly says bins parameter accepts a Series — it does not

The pd.cut() docstring states: 'bins: int, sequence of scalars, or Series'. Passing a Series raises TypeError: bins must be monotonically increasing or decreasing. The docstring should say 'array-like' or explicitly list the supported types.
label: docs

text:
Update DataFrame.swaplevel() docs to reflect that the default axis is 0 not None

The API reference page for DataFrame.swaplevel() lists the default value of the axis parameter as None, but the actual default is 0 (row axis). The discrepancy confuses users who try to call swaplevel() on columns without specifying axis=1.
label: docs

text:
Add deprecation warning to DataFrame.bool() in the docstring — method is deprecated since 2.1

DataFrame.bool() was deprecated in 2.1.0 but the docstring only mentions this in the Changelog. Users reading the API reference have no indication the method is deprecated. Add a prominent DeprecationWarning note at the top of the docstring.
label: docs

text:
Document that Index.append() creates a new Index and does not modify in place

Many users assume Index.append() behaves like list.append() and modifies the index in place. The docstring should explicitly state that a NEW Index is returned and that the original is unchanged, to prevent the silent bug of writing idx.append(new_vals) without reassigning.
label: docs

text:
Missing note in read_fwf() docs about how whitespace-only rows are handled

read_fwf() silently skips rows that contain only whitespace. This behaviour is not documented anywhere in the API reference. Users dealing with fixed-width files that have blank separator lines are surprised when row counts don't match expectations.
label: docs

text:
Wrong example in to_datetime() docs: example with utc=True produces tz-naive output

The first code example in the pd.to_datetime() docstring under the utc=True section shows output without timezone info, which contradicts the documented behaviour. The example should show the correct UTC-aware Timestamps.
label: docs

text:
how do I filter rows where a column value is in a list?

I have a list of ids and want to keep only rows where df['id'] is in that list. What is the pandas equivalent of SQL's WHERE id IN (1,2,3)?
label: question

text:
What is the correct way to avoid SettingWithCopyWarning when doing chained assignments?

I keep getting SettingWithCopyWarning even when I think I'm modifying the original DataFrame. I've read about .copy() but I'm not sure when to use it. Can someone explain the rule?
label: question

text:
Is pd.DataFrame.values safe to use for extracting a numpy array from a mixed-dtype DataFrame?

I need a numpy array from a DataFrame that has both int and float columns. Should I use .values, .to_numpy(), or np.array(df)? Are there differences in behaviour for mixed dtypes?
label: question

text:
how to merge two dataframes on multiple columns?

what is the syntax for joining df1 and df2 on both 'key1' and 'key2' columns at the same time?
label: question

text:
How do I convert a DataFrame column from Unix epoch integers to datetime?

`pd.to_datetime(df['ts'])` doesn't work when the column contains Unix timestamps as integers (seconds since 1970-01-01). What is the correct call to parse these as UTC datetimes?
label: question

text:
What happens when I use groupby on a column with NaN values — are NaN keys included?

I noticed that groupby silently drops rows where the grouping column is NaN. Is this the documented behaviour? Is there a way to include NaN as its own group?
label: question

text:
How to reset MultiIndex to regular columns after groupby aggregation?

After df.groupby(['a','b']).agg({'c':'sum'}), the result has a MultiIndex. What is the cleanest way to flatten this back to a regular DataFrame with 'a', 'b', 'c' as columns?
label: question

text:
What is the difference between DataFrame.copy(deep=True) and DataFrame.copy(deep=False)?

I need to know whether modifying a column of a shallow copy also modifies the original DataFrame, and in which cases I should use deep=False for performance.
label: question

text:
How do I apply a custom function to each element of a DataFrame efficiently?

I have a function that maps one string to another. Should I use df.applymap(), df.apply(lambda x: x.map(...)), or df.transform()? What are the performance differences between these approaches?
label: question

text:
Can I use pandas read_csv to load only specific rows based on a condition without loading the full file?

My CSV is 10 GB and I only need rows where column 'status' equals 'active'. Is there a way to filter while reading rather than loading everything into memory first? Or do I need to use chunking?
label: question

text:
How do I suppress FutureWarning messages globally in my pandas scripts?

My scripts produce many FutureWarning messages about deprecated behaviour. I know I should fix them eventually, but for now I want to suppress them. What is the correct way to filter these warnings in a pandas context?
label: question

text:
How to select all columns that start with a specific prefix?

I have a DataFrame with 100 columns and many of them start with 'feat_'. What is the most idiomatic way to select only those columns as a subset DataFrame?
label: question
